title: Container health checks
description: Configure Docker HEALTHCHECK instructions, understand startup versus liveness versus readiness probes, and use health checks to make your orchestrator self-healing.

data.text: A running container is not necessarily a healthy container. A process can be alive but deadlocked, listening but not serving, or starting but not yet ready. Health checks give Docker and your orchestrator the ability to distinguish a running container from a working one, and to restart or reroute traffic automatically when something goes wrong.

Docker has one native health check concept: the `HEALTHCHECK` instruction in a Dockerfile. Kubernetes expands this into three separate probes: `startupProbe`, `livenessProbe`, and `readinessProbe`. Each probe answers a different question about the container's state.

rows: Is the application still alive and responsive?
Is the application ready to serve traffic?

data.text: The `HEALTHCHECK` instruction tells Docker how to test whether a container is healthy. Docker runs the health check command at the interval you specify. If the command succeeds, the container is `healthy`. If it fails too many times, the container is marked `unhealthy`.

data.title: HTTP health check for a Node.js API
data.content: This Dockerfile uses curl to check the /health endpoint every 30 seconds.
data.code:
FROM node:20-alpine

RUN apk add --no-cache curl

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1

data.title: TCP health check for a database
data.content: For services that do not expose an HTTP endpoint, use a TCP connection check.
data.code:
FROM postgres:16-alpine

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
  CMD pg_isready -U "$POSTGRES_USER" || exit 1

data.title: HEALTHCHECK options
items: --timeout: maximum time to wait for a check to complete, default 30s
--start-period: grace period after container start, default 0s
--retries: number of consecutive failures before marking unhealthy, default 3
NONE: disable the default health check inherited from the base image

data.text: In Kubernetes, probes are configured in the Pod spec. The `startupProbe` runs first and disables the liveness and readiness probes until it succeeds. This gives slow-starting applications time to initialize without being killed prematurely.

data.title: Kubernetes probes for a web API
data.content: A Pod spec with startup, liveness, and readiness probes.
data.code:
containers:
  - name: api
    image: myapp:latest
    ports:
      - containerPort: 3000
    startupProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health/startup
        port: 3000
      failureThreshold: 30
      periodSeconds: 2
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health/live
        port: 3000
      failureThreshold: 3
      periodSeconds: 10
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health/ready
        port: 3000
      failureThreshold: 3
      periodSeconds: 5

data.title: Design your health endpoints
data.text: Expose at least two endpoints: one for startup or deep dependency checks and one for liveness. A readiness endpoint should verify the database connection, cache availability, and any other dependency the container needs to serve traffic.

data.title: What to avoid
items: Using the root URL as a health check when it triggers side effects such as sending email or writing logs
Setting the interval too low, which causes unnecessary load on the application
Setting the timeout too high, which delays detection of genuinely failed containers
Forgetting the startup period for applications that take more than a few seconds to initialize
Running the health check as a command that always returns success, which defeats the purpose

data.title: Key takeaways
points: A running process is not the same as a healthy application
Use HEALTHCHECK in Dockerfiles for standalone Docker deployments
Use Kubernetes probes for fine-grained startup, liveness, and readiness control
Design dedicated /health endpoints that do not trigger side effects
Give slow-starting applications a generous startup period before liveness checks begin
data.takeaway: Health checks are the difference between a container that restarts itself and one that quietly fails to serve traffic.
